To give you an idea, think about the differences between General American English and Scottish or Jamaican English. Every language speaks about the same pace. But the pace is measured by sentences, not syllables! Spanish needs more syllables for a sentence, so they "speak faster." Opposite is true e.g. for Finnish. So Finnish will sound sluggish to your ears.
You have to say a long sentence to mean the same thing as a short english sentence. So people just speed up their speech.

When in a social setting with Spanish speaking friends, we've been told we speak too fast. It's an excitability thing combined with being comfortable with each other. Ultimately, you need to listen to any language frequently so that your brain and your ears can get used to the speed, sounds, rhythm or cadence. Once you're comfortable you'll start picking up words and the speed won't feel as noticeable.
